propositions: A committed lock freezes transitive dependencies, causing any future advisory on a pinned transitive dep to block CI gating for all in-flight changes regardless of authorship or relevance
Unconditional pip-audit gating on advisory findings incorrectly punishes developers whose changes do not touch the dependency map, when advisory triage belongs to the lock owner on a main-branch lane
The retry logic in pip-audit only retries DB-unreachable failures, making `recheck` ineffective for real findings and creating time waste as authors reflexively attempt it

Developers incorrectly diagnose upstream caps as upgrade-impossible by misinterpreting `constraint-dependencies` UNSATISFIABLE output as proof, when the correct remedy is `override-dependencies` with justification
A periodic mechanism must notice when an `override-dependencies` escape-hatch suppression's REMOVE-WHEN condition is met, preventing stale overrides from silently outliving their justification
Gerrit verify must block on advisory only when the change touches the dependency map, while scheduled main-lane runs must fail visibly and route to an owner via automatic ticket filing with dedup
